<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Create a task and place it in the pool"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/tasks"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Puts a new unit of Pick, Pack, or SLAM work into the pending pool. The task is not assigned to any station at creation time — PULL dispatch (`POST /stations/{stationId}/task-claims`) is the only way a task becomes claimed, consistent with this service's rule that work is never pushed to a named station in advance. `cpt` (Critical Pull Time) drives dispatch priority: `claimNext` always selects the earliest-CPT pending task a station is equipped for.

**Idempotent per `Idempotency-Key` (ADR-0028).** Send a caller-chosen `Idempotency-Key` header on every call. The first request with a given key creates the task; a retry with the same key and the same body replays the stored response verbatim (same status, headers and task id — including a cached 4xx) instead of creating a duplicate. Reusing a key with a different body is rejected with `409 idempotency-key-reused`; omitting the header is `400 idempotency-key-required`. Postgres is the only runtime, so the check is on in every deployment. Without a repeated key every call creates a new task with a fresh, server-generated id.
